title: lfp lowerStar of surjective closed
statement:
theorem lfp_lowerStar_of_surjective_closed
    (Λ : Sheaf (coherentTopology Profinite.{u}) Ab.{u + 1})
    [MonObj Λ] [IsCommMonObj Λ] {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] [Surjective i]
    (P : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology Z) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj Λ Z))
    (hP : IsLocallyFinitelyPresented (condensedRingObj Λ Z) P) :
    IsLocallyFinitelyPresented (condensedRingObj Λ X)
      ((CondensedRing.lowerStar Λ i).obj P). This is the exact Lean statement, with the definitions cited in stmt_deps.

source.place: Tags 09AA, 09AH, 09AB; closed support and topological invariance

proof.text: Refine the given pro-etale presentation cover by one obtained from X. Keep the cartesian square as scheme-and-morphism data, so the presentation argument uses an abstract scheme instead of unfolding the chosen scheme pullback.

Finite presentations are invariant under isomorphisms and are preserved by additive functors preserving finite colimits and the regular module: transport the two finite free modules and their cokernel presentation. An equivalence preserving the regular module also reflects this property by applying its additive inverse.

Normalize each presentation and pull it back along the refinement map. The composition comparison and cartesian-square equation, followed by the closed counit, identify it with the pullback of the restriction of i_*P. Pullback along the base-changed surjective closed immersion is an equivalence preserving the regular module, so it reflects finite presentation. Undo coefficient normalization to obtain the presentations on the cover of X.

mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits about etale pretopologies, etale morphisms and surjective singleton covers; no pro-etale closed-immersion model or covering-refinement theorem. The source library affine ind-etale closed-site lift supplies the missing geometry.
Twelve hits, including Surjective.of_comp and stability and iso instances. These support the geometric arguments but do not state finite-model transport or pro-etale cover lifting.

Twenty-five hits, including closed embeddings on prime spectra and the fact that a surjective closed immersion into a reduced scheme is an isomorphism. No pro-etale covering or module-presentation result.
